result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers put the fixes in the same sensible order: the decline wipe first, then the silent grey button, then the early errors. Both give concrete wording for error messages. B is slightly better: it keeps more of what the customer typed after a decline (only the CVV is cleared, where A also clears the card number), it gives a clear blur-validation rule, and its funnel checks tell the PM which cause is driving the drop. Neither answer says to show the actual reason a card was declined. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers rank the fixes the same sensible way: the decline wipe first, then the disabled button, then the early error. Both treat placeholder-only labels as a smaller issue but still recommend visible labels. B's replacement error text, "Enter the 16-digit number on the front of your card", is more useful because it tells people how to fix the problem, and B also covers keyboard and screen-reader users and clearing errors once fixed. Neither answer fully asks for the real decline reason to be shown, and B wrongly says the page code wasn't shared, though it was.
